Definition: from G5497; to be a hand-leader, i.e. to guide (a blind person):--lead by the hand.
BiblicalUsage: To lead by the hand is the word for Saul after the light on the Damascus road: he rises from the earth blind, and they lead him by the hand into Damascus. Paul tells the same story again in Jerusalem, led by the hand of those with him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the proud persecutor had to be led like a child, and that is how God begins His work in him.
